# odyssey-104 (21.207–319): reviewer's record

Files read: runbook section 2, conventions.md (the house-rendering table was searched row by row for every Greek word and English house word in this part; the prose sections and the 21.x and 8.x blocks were read in full), packet.md, units.json, new-renderings.md, drafts/odyssey-001/units.json, known-forms.json and gloss.json, and, for cross-checks, the published parts 001–103 (Greek, `l`, `i`, `n` of the units that share words or lines with this part). No modern translation was opened or recalled. Edits were made to units.json only, by script (`t` untouched, checked unit by unit; the units still reproduce packet.md line by line, `ln` and `p` verified against the packet). 24 field edits in all (22 in pass 1, 2 in pass 2).

Counts. Pass 1 on the drafter's file: 0 High, 8 Medium, 13 Low. Pass 2 on the edited units.json: 0 High, 0 Medium, 2 Low. Pass 2 on gloss.json (not edited; for the lead): 0 High, 5 Medium, 6 Low.

## Gloss check (pass 2; gloss.json exists, not edited)

106 novel forms, 106 entries; 15 `__broaden__` entries, each beginning with the existing entry whole plus " · ". All parses were read against the line. These need the lead's attention (all in gloss.json):

Medium
- κληῗσαι, προβλώσκειν, ἰῆλαι, ἐπιτρέψαι: each entry says "standing for an imperative". In this part none of them is: κληῗσαι depends on εἰπεῖν (236) and on ἐπιτέλλομαι (241), προβλώσκειν on εἰπεῖν (239), ἰῆλαι on ἐπιτέλλομαι (241), ἐπιτρέψαι on λίσσομ' (279). Suggested: "aor. inf. act. … : 'to shut'" / "pres. inf., in an indirect command: '(tell them) not to go out'" / "aor. inf. act. …: 'to throw (on)'" / "aor. inf. act., after λίσσομαι: 'to entrust'".
- παῦσαι (known entry, "aor. imper. mid. 2 sg.: 'cease!'"): the note and the pass-1 resolution read 279 as the aorist infinitive 'make cease' with accusative τόξον, so the existing entry does not cover this use. It should go under `__broaden__`: old entry whole, then " · also aor. inf. act., 'to make cease': νῦν μὲν παῦσαι τόξον 'let the bow rest'".

Low
- `__broaden__` χειρῶν: "'trial of (your) hands'" — the hands are the speaker's own; use "(one's own)" or "(my)".
- τιταίνοιτ: "stretch, draw (a bow)" and "'would string'" clash with the table (τιταίνω is 'stretch'/'bend a bow'; "draw" is avoided, and 'string' is the ἐντανύω word). Suggested "stretch, strain (a bow) … 'would bend'".
- κέλεσθε: "'bid!'" — 'bid' is reserved for ἄνωγα; use 'urge!'.
- ἀεσίφρονι and ἐπητύος: the notes say the meaning is not known (known only by guess), the entries do not; the convention is that an uncertain meaning is said to be so.
- ἔξοχοι: "'outstanding among'" — 'outstanding' is reserved for ἀριπρεπής; 'standing out above' follows the table.

Checked and fine: lemma, case, number, tense, mood and voice of all other novel entries; the `__broaden__` additions for σῆμα, βαλόντε, ἴδηται, δόμεναι, ἢ, αὐτοῦ, περί, αἱ, κε, τοσσόνδε, δαιτὸς, αἴσιμα, ἀπ, ἐντανύσῃ; the uses of ἦ, ἤ, ὅ, ὃ, μετά (adverb 'afterwards', 231), ἔνθεν, πάρος, τανύσσαι and ἕζετ' are covered by their existing entries.

## Drafter's flagged items — resolutions

- κράτος "power" (280). Kept. The only κράτος row (11.353) fixes "power" and lists "might" as avoided; the sentence "'might' (reserved for κράτος)" in the ἲς row (11.393) contradicts it, and the shipped parts are mixed (strength 001/043, mastery and authority 004, might 022, power 054). For the conventions table: copy the new row as written, and strike "(reserved for κράτος)" from the ἲς row or reword it, so that the table no longer reserves "might" for a word it also lists "might" as avoided for.
- ἔειπε (278) subject. Left as the note has it ("not named, presumably Antinous, who spoke last"). The verb is singular and both men are begged; Antinous spoke last and is the one who proposed putting the contest off, and `i` puts "he" directly after his name. Not certain, and the note says so.
- παῦσαι (279). Resolved as an infinitive (see pass 1, line 277) and the note rewritten; the gloss entry needs broadening (above).
- Uncertain etymologies and meanings (προμνηστῖνοι, ἀεσίφρων, ἐπητύς, χανδόν, ἀτέμβειν, ἀκομιστίη, οἰνοβαρείων, ἐΰξοον, δαΐφρων). Each is said to be uncertain or rare in its note with the house wording; checked against the table rows. The only gap is in the gloss (ἀεσίφρων, ἐπητύς).
- κληΐς "key" vs "bolt" (236, 241). Kept "bolt". The only published κληΐς for a fastening is 102.5 "a well-bent key" (the storeroom, 21.6) and 090.293 "hooks"; the courtyard doors are a different object, the note says so, and the new row records it. No published part has a door κληΐς, so nothing contradicts.

## Findings considered and refused

- τανύσσαι (254) rendered "string" although the new τιταίνω row says "string" is reserved for ἐντανύω. Refused: odyssey-103 (21.171) ships "cannot string it" for the same word, and the table has τανυστύς "the stringing"; changing it would put 104 against 103. Suggest rewording the row's avoided column to "string (the ἐντανύω word, but shipped for the simplex τανύσσαι at 21.171 — τιταίνω itself stays 'bend')".
- ὡς after γιγνώσκω (209) 'that' vs 'how'. Both read; the note's 'that' is acceptable.
- ἐνὶ θυμῷ (218) singular in `l`, "hearts" in `i`: the `i` plural distributes over two persons; `l` stays literal.
- "arms" for χεῖρε (223) against "hands" for χεῖρας (225): ἀμφὶ … χεῖρε βαλόντε is the idiom for an embrace (053.210 ships "arms … thrown"); the note says 'two arms'.
- "ἔλδομαι" (209 note) for the lemma of ἐελδομένοισιν: ἔλδομαι/ἐέλδομαι are one verb; the gloss uses ἐέλδομαι; left.
- `l` of 268 puts "we" at the end of its third line (the Greek 'we' is in line 4): follows the published 268 wording the validator would otherwise enforce for line 4, and "coherence wins ties".
- "today" (258) for νῦν in `i`, "Meanwhile" (245) for δέ, "No," (259) for ἀλλά, "From that time" (303): all within the `i` register and each contrast (νῦν μὲν … ἠῶθεν δὲ) is kept.
- "carry off" in `i` against "take up" in `l` (261): ἀναιρέομαι covers both, the note says so.
- ἐρίδαινε (310) "strive" in `l`, "compete" in `i`, while 006 ships "vie"/"competing" and 091 "quarrelling" for forms of the same verb. The published parts do not agree among themselves, so no house wording exists to enforce.
- "pushed away" for ἀποέργαθεν (221): `l` and `i` agree and 011 ships "keeps off" for the present stem with a thing as object; a person's hand clearing rags is "pushed away".
- Remembered English: nothing in `i` read as a recalled phrase; the few phrases that came readily ("yet to come to hear of", "weighed down with wine", "pliant limbs") were each rebuilt from the Greek (ἐσσομένοισι πυθέσθαι, the house row, γναμπτός 'bent, flexible') and left.
- Scansion flags: none in the packet, so no line was hand-scanned for irregularity.
- Segmentation: units end at full stops, question marks and raised dots; the four-line sentence at 222–225 is the stated exception (no stop printed after ὤμους, and the note says so).
